description: The agent must: (1) Read the SKILL.md to understand the three key rules: full citation-style consistency, page-number pinpointing requirement, and correct supra note numbering. (2) Parse the memorial text and identify: STYLE VIOLATIONS — footnotes 4 (Bluebook treaty format), 5 (APA format), and 7 (Bluebook case format) break the consistency rule because the rest of the document uses OSCOLA; PAGE NUMBER VIOLATIONS — footnote 8 (Gabcikovo case has no pinpoint page) and footnote 12 (Milanovic journal article has no pinpoint page); SUPRA NOTE ERRORS — footnote 16 says 'Nicaragua (n 2)' but Nicaragua was first cited at FN1; footnote 18 says 'Corfu Channel (n 9)' but Corfu was first cited at FN2; footnote 20 says 'Cassese (n 11)' but Cassese was first cited at FN5; footnote 22 says 'Vienna Convention (n 7)' but the VCLT was first cited at FN6. (3) Critically, the agent must NOT falsely flag correct supra notes: FN11 'Nicaragua (n 1)' is correct, and FN14 'Shaw (n 3)' is also correct (Shaw was indeed first cited at FN3). (4) Output all findings as citation_audit_report.json. The proprietary trap: a generic agent may not know the OSCOLA-specific supra note rule (pointing to the FIRST footnote where a source appeared), the requirement to include specific page pinpoints, or the Jessup-specific guidance that mixing styles (even between equally-valid styles) is the cardinal sin.
